To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the critical points in the schema matching problem can be identified, (2) the matching algorithm can be made more accurate by incorporating the context, and (3) a prototype system can be built which performs well in practice

(a) the best schema matching algorithms use multiple matching methods, (b) the context in which elements are embedded in schemas is a powerful indicator of semantic relationships, (c) user feedback is most useful in identifying the critical points in a match, and (d) schema matching is a difficult and challenging problem, with no algorithm that performs optimally across all schemas

the context provided by paths and by the way elements occur in paths is very important, and that a schema matching algorithm should not be too greedy, but should leave some critical points to be handled by the user, in a user friendly way.
